page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is an entry-level GPU-accelerated instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, providing 4 GB per core. For acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA Pascal-based P4 GPU with 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included, and network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance sits on the lower end of modern cloud compute capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is categorized as poor, falling in the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance is weak, in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests, including both small-block cached and large-block uncached reads and writes, consistently rank in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET performance are weak, reflecting the older Broadwell CPU architecture and memory subsystem. However, the Passmark CPU score achieves an average rating, indicating acceptable performance for standard non-parallelized compute tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge offers a qualitative entry point for GPU-accelerated computing without the premium associated with newer-generation architectures. Because it utilizes older Intel Xeon and NVIDIA Pascal hardware, it is best suited for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not demand high memory bandwidth or modern CPU instruction sets. Appropriate workloads include light machine learning inference, legacy CUDA-based applications, video transcoding, and general-purpose tasks requiring modest parallel processing capabilities.
